design_rationale: This was an individually randomized controlled trial using an independent centralized web-based system with a computer algorithm and minimization by age, sex, and baseline OME severity.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated and implemented through an independent centralized web-based service, with minimization on prespecified prognostic factors, providing adequate sequence generation and concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An independent external agency provided a centralised web-based randomisation system (www.sealedenvelope.com) for nurses to access while recruiting children to the study. The randomisation used an algorithm with minimisation based on three potential effect modifiers/confounders: age (< 6.5 years vs. > 6.5 years), sex and baseline severity of OME.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, families, and nurses knew allocation in this open behavioral trial, which could affect adherence, co-interventions, or parent-reported outcomes, although compliance was high and the main analysis was intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Owing to the nature of the intervention, use of placebo was not possible and therefore nurses, children and families were not masked to treatment allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome data were missing for a meaningful proportion of randomized children (approximately 18% at 1 month and 23% at 3 months), although losses were similar between arms and multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis was reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At 1 month, the proportion of children with normal tympanograms was 47.3% (62/131) in those allocated to autoinflation and 35.6% (47/132) in those receiving usual care... At 3 months, the proportions were 49.6% (62/125) and 38.3% (46/120), respectively.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was an objective, consistently defined tympanometric measure, and post-randomization tympanograms were anonymized and interpreted by experts blinded to treatment assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Tympanometry outcomes at 1 and 3 months were anonymised by the Primary Care and Vaccines Collaborative Clinical Trials Unit and assessed blind by an expert panel.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, outcomes and time points were prespecified, and analyses followed an analysis plan with disclosed changes, leaving little indication that the primary result was selectively chosen.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trial registration: Current Controlled Trials ISRCTN55208702.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by the open-label design and appreciable missing primary outcome data. These concerns are mitigated by centralized randomization, blinded expert assessment of the objective primary outcome, intention-to-treat analysis, sensitivity analyses, and prospective trial registration.

design_rationale: This was an explicitly randomized controlled trial: after stratification by ability to open the eustachian tubes, subjects were assigned to autoinflation or observation using a set of random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: A random-number sequence and stratification were reported and measured baseline characteristics were broadly comparable, but allocation concealment was not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Within each stratification, subjects were randomly assigned to either the autoinflation or the control group by the use of a set of random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and parents necessarily knew assignment, adherence relied on parent-recorded score cards with no adherence results reported, and the analysis excluded one randomized control participant rather than clearly applying intention-to-treat, although no control participant reported crossover.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Parents were asked to record the number of "exercise" cycles completed each day and turn in the score card at the end of the 2-week study as a method to monitor patient compliance.

domain_judgments.rationale: Two-week outcome data were available for 40 of 41 randomized participants (97.6%), with only one control participant missing, so bias from missing outcome data is unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 40 subjects evaluated at the two-week endpoint, only 3 subjects (7.5 percent) were effusion-free; 1 in the inflation group and 2 in the control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Resolution of effusion was assessed consistently using otologic examination and tympanometry, but assessor blinding was not reported and knowledge of assignment could have influenced the partly clinician-assessed endpoint.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All subjects received an otologic examination and tympanogram at each of the two weekly follow-up visits.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prespecified protocol or statistical analysis plan was reported, and several possible outcome time points and middle-ear status analyses were available, leaving some potential for selective reporting despite a clearly stated primary two-week comparison.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The proportions of children who were effusion-free at 2 weeks were compared in the two study groups by use of the Fisher's exact test.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The main issues are unreported allocation concealment and outcome-assessor blinding, limited information on adherence and intention-to-treat analysis, and absence of a prespecified protocol; missing outcome data were minimal.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that 100 children were randomized to autoinflation or observation, although the sequence-generation method is not described.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random allocation is stated and measured baseline histories were reportedly similar, but the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods are not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients were randomized to either a group performing autoinflation for 2 weeks or to a group being observed without treatment for 2 weeks.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew their treatment, adherence varied, and the principal between-group comparison excluded randomized children who did not perform autoinflation as prescribed rather than using an intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Comparison of the two groups included only those children who had performed autoinflation as prescribed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were unavailable for some randomized children by 2 weeks and progressively fewer ears were observed through 90 days, without reasons or analyses showing that missingness could not bias the results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 50 children randomized to the autoinflation group, 20 girls and 26 boys (median age, 5.3 years) attended, as a minimum, the first three trials... Of the 50 children in the control group, 19 girls and 28 boys... attended at least the three first trials.

domain_judgments.rationale: Tympanometry is an appropriate objective outcome and appears to have been applied similarly, but assessor blinding is not reported and knowledge of assignment could potentially influence test conduct or interpretation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Otomicroscopy and tympanometry were performed after 2 weeks (at visit 3), after 1 month (visit 4), after 2 months (visit 5), and after 3 months (visit 6).

domain_judgments.rationale: No prespecified protocol or analysis plan is reported, and results were analyzed across several visits, tympanogram subgroups, and outcome formulations, allowing potential selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Tympanometry was repeated at 2 weeks and at 1, 2, and 3 months after the children were entered into the study.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because the main comparison excluded nonadherent randomized participants and outcome data were missing for randomized children with substantial attrition over follow-up. Unreported allocation concealment, assessor blinding, and prespecification add further concerns.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated using a centralized Web-based computer-generated randomization system with minimization based on age, sex, and baseline severity.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer generated and centrally administered by an independent agency, providing concealment until nurse access, and key baseline characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An independent external agency provided a centralized Web-based computer-generated randomization system (www.sealedenvelope.com) for nurses to access while recruiting children.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, families, and nurses knew allocation, so behavior or co-interventions could have differed, although compliance was high and the modified intention-to-treat analysis retained participants regardless of reported compliance while excluding those without measurable outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Because of the nature of the intervention, use of placebo was not possible, and therefore nurses, children and families were not masked to treatment allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was modest but reached 12.2% at 3 months, and the complete-case primary estimate was attenuated and became statistically nonsignificant under multiple imputation, indicating some potential sensitivity to missing outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Retention was good, with 8.4% lost to follow-up at 1 month and 12.2% at 3 months... Sensitivity analyses using multiple imputation for missing data yielded similar but slightly smaller RRs that did not achieve statistical significance.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was an objective, validated tympanometric measure applied consistently, with anonymized printouts independently reviewed by allocation-masked experts and disagreements adjudicated by a third audiologist.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two members of the trial team, trained in tympanometry and masked to allocation, independently reviewed anonymized tympanometry printouts.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, its protocol was available, and analyses were conducted according to a prespecified analysis plan, with the defined primary outcome reported at both planned follow-up times.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Analyses were conducted using SAS version 9.3 and Stata version 13.0 according to a prespecified analysis plan.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by the open-label design and modest missing outcome data whose imputation attenuated the primary estimates. Randomization and allocation concealment were robust, and the objective primary outcome was assessed by masked experts under a prespecified analysis plan.

design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that the 60 patients were 'randomly divided into two groups,' which constitutes reported random allocation, although the sequence-generation and concealment methods are not described.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although random allocation is stated and age/sex were reported as similar, the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods are not described, and baseline comparability was only sparsely reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients were randomly divided into two groups

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and caregivers necessarily knew whether autoinflation was used, treatment interruptions occurred during respiratory infections, adherence was only described qualitatively, and no intention-to-treat or other estimand-based analysis was reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eleven children who had upper respiratory tract infection ceased the autoinflation for 5 days but autoinflation treatment was completed to 6 weeks.

domain_judgments.rationale: Approximately 11–12% of ears were reported lost to follow-up, with no reasons by group or sensitivity analysis establishing that missingness could not bias the results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 6 ears (12%) were lost in follow-up and in control group; ... 5 ears (11%) were lost in follow-up

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessment included clinician-determined persistence/clearance of effusion and need for ventilation-tube insertion, but assessor blinding was not reported; knowledge of treatment could influence these partly judgment-based outcomes, and analyzing ears rather than randomized children also ignores within-child correlation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients in both groups were examined with pneumatic otoscopy and tympanogram once every two weeks for the first two months and then once a month for 7 months.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prespecified protocol or statistical analysis plan is reported, while several outcomes and time points were measured, leaving scope to select among eligible measurements or analyses; the tables also contain internally inconsistent denominators/percentages.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Examinations were recorded at 6th week, 3rd, 6th, and 9th month.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because the unreported assessor blinding could materially influence the clinician-determined effusion and ventilation-tube outcomes. Additional concerns arise from unspecified randomization/concealment, incomplete follow-up without sensitivity analysis, lack of a prespecified analysis plan, and analysis by ear despite randomization by child.

design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that eligible children were allocated at random to autoinflation or no treatment, although the sequence-generation method is not described.

domain_judgments.rationale: The authors report random allocation, but give no information on sequence generation, allocation concealment, or baseline comparability beyond overall age.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The children so selected were, with the informed consent of their parents, allocated at random into two groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and parents necessarily knew the assigned treatment, compliance was based on parental report, and the paper does not describe an intention-to-treat analysis or whether any post-randomization deviations occurred.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The parents reported good compliance with this technique.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome counts account for all 41 ears assigned to autoinflation and all 37 ears assigned to no treatment, with no reported loss to follow-up at three weeks.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In Group A, of the 41 ears investigated 37 showed no improvement... In Group B, of the 37 ears investigated, 27 showed no improvement.

domain_judgments.rationale: The same prespecified otoscopic, audiometric, and tympanometric assessments were used in both groups, but assessor blinding is not reported and knowledge of assignment could have influenced testing or interpretation; moreover, ears rather than randomized children were analyzed without accounting for within-child correlation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The children were reviewed after 3 weeks and had repeat otoscopy, pure tone audiogram and tympanogram.

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol, trial registration, or prespecified statistical analysis is reported, leaving possible selective choice among audiometric and tympanometric definitions or analyses, including the ear-level analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The ear was considered to have improved if: (1) There was an average improvement of 10 dB in the pure tone audiogram frequencies from 250–2000 Hz. (2) A peak appeared in a previously flat tympanogram.

overall_summary: Overall, the trial raises some concerns because sequence generation and allocation concealment, assessor blinding, intention-to-treat handling, and prospective analysis specification were not reported. Outcome data appear complete, but the ear-level analysis also failed to address clustering of two ears within some randomized children.

design_rationale: The 45 eligible children were explicitly allocated using computer-generated independent randomization sequences in blocks of six to treatment-first or control-first crossover groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated blocked sequence was used, but allocation concealment was not described and statistically significant baseline differences in age and hearing thresholds raise some concern despite otherwise credible randomization.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Computer-generated, independent allocation sequences were used for randomisation. To avoid disproportionate numbers of patients in each group, randomisation was performed in blocks of six subjects (three allocated to the treatment and three to the control group).

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and parents could not be blinded, some nonadherence was reported, and the analysis population and intention-to-treat handling during the randomized phase were not fully clear, although weekly follow-up and diaries monitored compliance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In one case, the compliance was not satisfactory to complete the four-week treatment. Some parents reported partial compliance failure described as “lack of time” to perform the exercise, especially in the mornings.

domain_judgments.rationale: Reported ear counts suggest some unavailable audiometric measurements and participant denominators vary, but missingness by randomized group and reasons are not transparently reported, so its effect on the primary eight-week results is uncertain.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Pure tone audiometry was performed in all children, except for those that would not collaborate in the performance of this examination. These children performed sound field audiometry instead.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary tympanometric and audiometric outcomes were objective, prespecified, assessed consistently with standardized equipment, and audiometry was conducted by an experienced assessor blinded to group allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Pure tone air conduction thresholds for each ear or sound field audiometry for both ears were performed by an experienced audiologist who was blinded to the group allocation of the child.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or accessible prespecified analysis plan is reported, and multiple continuous and categorized outcome definitions and analyses were available, creating potential for selective reporting despite identification of primary outcomes and the main analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome measurements were improvement in middle-ear pressure and hearing thresholds at eight weeks.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by unclear allocation concealment, baseline imbalances, imperfectly documented adherence and missing outcome data, and lack of preregistration or an accessible prespecified analysis plan. Objective outcome measurement with blinded audiometry reduces concern in the measurement domain.
